We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid (C=C). 3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give acid and aniline (aniline attached to phenyl). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: amide bond between carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl) and aniline (aniline with NH2). So precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl (i.e., Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1? Wait the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring via /C=C/COOH? Actually target has /C=C/C(=O)N... So the acid precursor would be Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1 (i.e., replace amide with carboxylic acid). Then second step: Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. The aldehyde would be aromatic aldehyde attached to sulfonyl phenyl: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1. So precursor 2: aromatic aldehyde with sulfonyl phenyl. Third step: sulfonamide formation: from sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). So precursor 3: sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 and aniline (the other phenyl? Actually sulfonamide formed between sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the same phenyl? The sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring (the first ring). The amine partner is the second phenyl? Wait sulfonamide in target is NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl ring (first ring) and attached to second phenyl ring (c2...). So sulfonamide formed between sulfonyl chloride attached to first phenyl and aniline (the second phenyl). So precursor: first phenyl with sulfonyl chloride: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 and second phenyl with NH2: c2ccc(NH2)cc2? Actually the second phenyl is attached via sulfonamide to first phenyl, not via amide. In target, NS(=O)(=O) attached to first phenyl (para to methyl) and to second phenyl (para to the unsaturated chain). So the sulfonamide bond is between sulfonyl chloride on first phenyl and aniline (second phenyl). So precursor: first phenyl sulfonyl chloride (as above) and second phenyl amine (c2ccc(NH2)cc2). Then after sulfonamide formation we get sulfonamide attached phenyls. Then Doebner modification on the second phenyl (which now has sulfonamide attached) to install α,β-unsaturated acid. Then amide formation with aniline (c3ccccc3N) which is actually the same as the second phenyl? Wait the second phenyl after Doebner will have the unsaturated chain attached to it, and also the sulfonamide attached to it (the N of sulfonamide is attached to the second phenyl). The amide formation uses the aniline (c3ccccc3N) which is the same second phenyl? Actually the amide is attached to the unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N- phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (aniline). That phenyl is the same as the second phenyl? In target, the unsaturated chain ends with C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). That phenyl is not the same as the sulfonamide phenyl (c2...). The sulfonamide phenyl is attached to the sulfonyl group, not to the amide. So there are three phenyl rings: ring A (methyl phenyl with sulfonamide), ring B (phenyl attached to sulfonyl group and bearing the unsaturated chain), ring C (aniline attached to amide). So sulfonamide formed between ring A (sulfonyl chloride) and ring B (aniline). Then Doebner modification on ring B (which now has sulfonamide substituent) to create unsaturated acid attached to ring B. Then amide formation between that acid and ring C (aniline). So we need three steps.

Now we need to find templates for each transformation.

We have template for sulfonamide formation (maybe template ID 120747 earlier: C-S(=O)(=O)-N...). That is forward sulfonamide formation? The retro template is breaking sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and amine? Let's check template 120747: retro_smarts_template: '[C:2]-[NH;D2;+0:1]-[c:3]>>C-S(=O)(=O)-[N;H0;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[c:3]'. This is forward? The retro direction is from amide? Actually it shows product side left? The retro template transforms amine + sulfonyl? The left side is C-NH-c (anilide) to sulfonamide? Not sure. But we can use apply_template to see if it works.

We need to get template IDs for each step. Could search for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Search functional groups broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, formed: amide. Already attempted but got empty. Maybe need to search with functional_groups_formed: ["amide"] and broken: []? Let's try search for amide formation template.
